river: Tekerghat limestone quarry lakes and border quarries (Tahirpur)
note: Added from Google Maps (Niladri Lake). The abandoned limestone quarry lake predates the record; bare quarry ground spreads over the border slope from 2000 and peaks in 2010–2013 (bare 35 to 104–219 ha, break 2003, p < 0.001), then shrinks after 2019.
exclusion_reason: Rock quarry, not river sand or gravel extraction (Jim Best, 6 Nov 2026): Tekerghat limestone quarry lakes (Meghalaya border)

river: Lafarge Umiam limestone mine at Nongtrai (Meghalaya, India)
note: Added from Google Maps. Forested slope until 2003; the open-pit limestone mine that feeds the Chhatak cement plant by a cross-border conveyor appears in 2004–2005 (bare ground 8 to 41 ha after 2005, p < 0.001) and grows to about 50 ha by 2023–2025.
exclusion_reason: Rock quarry, not river sand or gravel extraction (Jim Best, 6 Nov 2026): Lafarge Umiam limestone mine, Nongtrai

river: Lafarge Surma cement plant and limestone yard (Chhatak)
note: Added from Google Maps. Wetland and fields until 2000; the plant and its limestone and clinker yard are cleared in 2001–2005 (bare ground to about 100 ha) and built over by 2010. Receives the limestone quarried at N39.
exclusion_reason: Rock quarry, not river sand or gravel extraction (Jim Best, 6 Nov 2026): Lafarge Surma cement plant limestone and clinker yard, Chhatak

river: Lumshnong limestone quarries and cement plants (Meghalaya, India)
note: Added from Google Maps (Star Cement and neighbouring plants, upstream of the Lukha and the Lubha). Forest in every January to 2003; quarry ground opens in 2004 to 2006 (bare ground 0–3 to 15–52 ha, p < 0.001) and keeps growing: about 65 ha in 2009–2014, 120–160 ha in 2019–2022 and 210–285 ha in 2023–2025. The largest and fastest-growing quarry in the belt.
exclusion_reason: Rock quarry, not river sand or gravel extraction (Jim Best, 6 Nov 2026): Lumshnong limestone quarries

river: Mawmluh limestone quarry at Sohra (Meghalaya, India)
note: Added from Google Maps; pit-field mode. The Mawmluh quarry predates the record (the Cherra cement plant opened in the 1960s), so there is no onset to date. The plateau series swings with grass burning and terrain shadow (mapped water 0–160 ha) and settles after 2011; no persistent rise of quarry ground.
exclusion_reason: Rock quarry, not river sand or gravel extraction (Jim Best, 6 Nov 2026): Mawmluh limestone quarry, Sohra

river: Cheragaon (Kalapani) stone quarry above Tahirpur border (Meghalaya, India)
note: Added from a Google imagery sweep (pit-field mode). A stone quarry on the forested slope just north of the Cheragaon border crossing, opposite the Tahirpur haor. Google Earth Historical Imagery shows forest in Aug 2011, Jan 2017, Apr 2018 and Dec 2019 and an open quarry of about 20 ha by Dec 2022. Landsat bare ground stays at 1–8 ha (with a road cut in 2010–2014) and rises to 14–20 ha in 2022–2025. The window holds only the northern part of the quarry, so the area is a lower bound.
exclusion_reason: Rock quarry, not river sand or gravel extraction (Jim Best, 6 Nov 2026): Cheragaon hill-slope stone quarry

note: Added from the Sentinel-2 change map (pit-field mode), 3 km north of the Lumshnong quarries (N65).
